sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for slide building
sections.what: Brings in the file system, path and checksum tools, the result type, the layout, the slide registry and the citations appendix.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps layout, slide choice and citations in their own files.
sections.watch_out: Names imported from the deck folder must stay in step with that folder, or this file will fail to load.

sections.name: require
sections.title: Loading the library and output folder
sections.what: Loads the PowerPoint library in a way that works with this project's module setup, and sets the folder where finished runs are saved.
sections.why: The code uses a module loader to load the library. The reason for this approach is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The output folder is relative to the launch folder, so the same code can save files in different places.

sections.name: renderRecipePptx
sections.title: Saved presentation builder
sections.what: Builds the full presentation for a run, draws every slide and the citations appendix, saves it under a name made from the run ID, and returns its location, checksum, slide count and warnings.
sections.why: The header says this is a thin wrapper, with slide content produced elsewhere.
sections.watch_out: The slide count returned is the appendix page count, which includes split pages, so it may differ from the number of slide entries.

sections.name: resolveArtifactAbsolute
sections.title: Full path helper
sections.what: Turns a relative file path into a full path, and leaves a path that is already full unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets other code accept either form of path.
sections.watch_out: A relative path is resolved against the current folder, so the same input can point somewhere else when the program starts elsewhere.

sections.name: renderRecipePptxBuffer
sections.title: In-memory presentation builder
sections.what: Builds the same presentation as the saved version but returns its raw bytes, so it can be sent or tested without writing to disk.
sections.why: The comment says it renders an isolated copy without replacing a recorded file.
sections.watch_out: It repeats the setup steps of the saved builder, so a change to one must be made in the other too.

summary: Builds the PowerPoint file for a Lessons Learnt run, either saved to disk or returned as bytes in memory.
purpose: Turns a finished result into a presentation the owner can download, with citation notes and links.
why: The header comments say branding sets the layout, the registry chooses which slides to draw, and this file holds no slide content of its own.
how: The saving version creates the output folder if needed, names the file after the run ID, applies the layout, sets the title and subject, builds the slide list for the run, draws each slide, adds the citations appendix, writes the file, and computes a SHA-256 checksum. The in-memory version does the same steps but returns the bytes and does not save a file.
inputs: A RecipeResult object and a run ID string.
outputs: The saving version returns the file path, a checksum, the slide count after splitting, and any warnings. The in-memory version returns the raw file bytes.
risks: The output folder is set relative to the folder the program starts from, so a different launch folder puts files in a different place. The author field is set to a fixed value in code. Warnings are written to the console as well as returned.
debug: If no file appears, check the output folder and write permissions. If slides are missing, read the returned warnings and the console. If the layout looks wrong, check that the layout step runs before any slide is added.
